eec0852073c0b81a0386: 1.3 · The role of players and the Game Master
0860c44a14094f348e48: 1.4 · The Will of D. System
7ae675d7ddaed4f94bd5: Grand Line Chronicles is a tabletop roleplaying game inspired by the world of One Piece, designed to let every player create their own pirate, join a crew and experience an adventure built together with the other players.
d8bc125470032ce4888f: Every character begins as more than a simple combination of statistics. They have an Ambition, an origin, a Race, particular abilities, a role within the crew and their own way of facing the world. Some fight on the front line, some helm the ship, some cook, some treat the wounded, some build machinery, and some interpret traces of the past. The crew works because each person brings something the others lack.
22664876420dec650fd0: One participant takes on the role of Game Master. The GM describes the world, portrays the characters encountered during the voyage, presents dangers, islands, opponents and opportunities, and determines the consequences of players' actions when the rules require a decision.
5167ff327aa83b2c63d5: There is no predetermined path to follow. Players declare what their characters want to do, the Game Master describes what happens and, when the outcome of an action is uncertain, the dice come into play.
8fbc470c24323a8ac672: The rules of Grand Line Chronicles therefore answer a simple question:
181342a61f00b2f6d2ad: “What happens when we do not already know how things will turn out?”
afd7174b1c9345a88722: Fighting an opponent, performing an impossible manoeuvre during a storm, administering desperate treatment, building a weapon, preparing a banquet or trying to cross an unknown island can all become moments in which the character's abilities and the dice roll determine the outcome.
d2d75bb2e8c38ad80b32: Grand Line Chronicles does not, however, separate the character from crew life. The game also includes what happens between battles: managing the ship, the Galley, the Workshop, the market, resources collected during the voyage and the growth of the different crew members.
81ba57ae80e76708961b: Characters do not grow only by becoming stronger in combat. They can become better navigators, cooks capable of supporting the whole crew, Engineers capable of building and maintaining tools, machinery and structures, or fighters capable of developing ever more extraordinary Techniques, Haki and abilities.
88974d732c1b25ed0150: At the heart of the game, however, is the crew.
7317847cf7138c3b31a2: A single character can be exceptional. A complete crew can cross the Grand Line.
a939a9631586c35da648: A game of Grand Line Chronicles begins with a conversation.
9bdb981b3400733ef224: The Game Master describes a situation, players decide how their characters react, and the world responds to their actions. As long as what happens is clear, there is no need to interrupt the story with a die roll.
66c66188f53c9403ef1c: A pirate opens an unlocked door? They open it.
2a399537c73e6f140a44: The cook prepares a simple dinner with ordinary ingredients and all the time they need? There is no need to test their ability.
5a4b9024918c83fe8198: The navigator consults a familiar route in calm conditions? The voyage can simply continue.
1f2a2979425adb41cce3: Dice come into play when an action's outcome is uncertain, when there is a real possibility of failure or when the result can have significant consequences.
7ac1577cc4c2d16926fb: The basic cycle of play is therefore:
280c03bf37988fb4d224: The GM describes the situation → the player declares what they want to do → decide whether a roll is needed → apply the abilities involved → roll the dice → the result changes the situation.
751bec6f700295b11f05: From that point, play continues from the new reality created by the outcome.
0ea1f71875b26363eec8: If a pirate tries to leap from one ship to another during a storm, the roll does more than determine whether they “succeed” or “fail”. The result can determine how they succeed, which position they reach, which risk they avoid or which problem arises from the attempt.
a104b158849b689e6474: Likewise, in combat, an attack is not an isolated event. Its result can deal damage, move an enemy, apply a condition, activate a Talent, prepare a subsequent attack or completely change the combatants' positions.
2b58666fd49181ab5512: The rules turn these consequences into something clear and shared.
1af655880de207f43ad7: Not every action requires a check.
faf03fdcdff7ebedd978: If there is no real uncertainty, the GM can simply describe the result.
2357c3f7b8c36baf54c0: A roll should be used when at least one possible consequence is significant. Failure must be capable of changing something.
3f090c6f955f47e9effc: This prevents the game from becoming an endless sequence of dice rolls and keeps attention on the moments that truly matter.
69ac3a9d998ae5020fa2: Even a highly experienced character can face a situation difficult enough to require a check. Likewise, a simple situation may not require one at all, regardless of the values of their characteristics.
5d49cb57da107d4b5d31: When a player wants to do something, they should first describe the character's intention, rather than choosing a rule directly.
de941a356322953ea4b2: “I want to run along the parapet and reach the Marine before they close the gate.”
1a0f31e63a6f19383b02: The first declaration tells the table what the character is actually trying to do. Only then do you determine which Attribute, Skill, Technique or other ability best represents that action.
3eb70ab997e2347aaa2a: This lets the same system handle very different situations without turning every scene into a list of buttons to press.
a15cef2f367e81b742f5: Every pirate has various tools for dealing with what they encounter.
dafd00af1bcdf9e9ffe6: Techniques represent particular actions developed by the character.
bce2efeb85bd0c461925: Weapons, Haki, Devil Fruits, equipment and other abilities can further modify what they can do.
fe79cbf67d01def358c1: Not all of these components contribute to the same roll. The rules in subsequent chapters explain when and how they can be used.
32f0bda88db127f50e5a: After a roll, the game should not return to exactly where it began.
dd2dd9f8827b28cb7399: A success allows the character to obtain what they sought or move closer to their goal.
bf0e5f05c95988542323: A failure introduces a consequence, a cost or a new difficulty, or leaves room for the opponent's response.
b6914459efaced56483d: The same principle holds in combat: each action progressively changes the battle by consuming resources, causing damage, changing positions or creating opportunities.
c48658f9eb14e50be03c: The die does not narrate the scene in the players' place.
8f1c46f1349432507f7f: It decides where the story must take a direction.
d15f0b1d90abf93da95b: In Grand Line Chronicles, everyone helps build the story, but not everyone has the same task.
35d2a275c910bb71f170: The Game Master portrays the rest of the world.
3ebcc110c1ff137f124a: This simple division supports the entire game.
55631d258367064ca6fe: Each player controls their own character.
2aa77780e6f9014a2b25: The character belongs to the player.
5e18728f8ce73a14e89f: The Game Master can describe what they perceive, what they suffer and the consequences of their actions, but should not decide for the player what they think, feel or choose to do.
c5887a57237ff2229787: A defeat can force a pirate to the ground.
ea153bf254b053f5f127: An enemy ability can prevent them from moving.
99d940e9598725f8ec68: A situation can make it impossible for them to reach an objective.
ff798ca192745902e259: But as long as the character retains the ability to choose, that choice remains in the player's hands.
272c61d1cd06ee900847: Grand Line Chronicles is built around different characters sharing the same adventure.
3e153d9bd793b4be7ee6: Not everyone needs to be an excellent fighter.
f46bc7512a20f6771b0e: A character can stand out because they know how to navigate, build, heal, cook, interpret ancient evidence or hold the crew together in its darkest moments.
207069bd5fa7da90b464: This means the game should not always revolve around the same type of check.
357259f550c64179a0dc: A good adventure alternates situations in which different crew members can make the difference.
35454b2958d52fc48d6c: During a storm, the Navigator might guide everyone.
63e15ae30ef9549c79cf: After a battle, the Doctor might prevent the consequences from becoming permanent.
a96c900fc02da9efbc7a: A seemingly useless object might become valuable in an Engineer's hands.
7917b2239b2e0f2446b0: An incomprehensible inscription might change the meaning of an entire island thanks to the Archaeologist.
2c626a6fa013041bb0a9: In combat, the same logic still applies: different characters face the battle with different tools.
5288a5871987602a6520: The crew is not a collection of sheets.
00aeebb12725b576111a: The Game Master is the voice of the world.
1c41b965c6a4c45ecdf2: They describe places, people, dangers, creatures and consequences.
5880a8b2f5f71585453e: everything that does not belong directly to the players.
1a5c2bd6b9bf2ff0b4ca: They are also responsible for presenting situations that require decisions.
8408fcb7414a207f4a57: They do not determine how the story will end.
ee48205e68b58b6119a6: They must create something the players can react to.
eb2b5746ff5cb0a46b1e: An island can have an ongoing conflict.
5db08e442f98211316e2: An antagonist can have a plan.
d51c8fcbb0ad350dcca1: A rival crew can be seeking the same treasure.
b4412b09bd456958d5b3: But what happens depends on what the characters do.
9a84eea84e7a34d4b36c: When a situation is clearly covered by the rules, the Game Master applies them.
3cbf4c269360dada62ec: When something arises that the system does not describe exactly, the GM decides how to represent it using the existing rules.
96d557c5640f280e4478: how to interpret an unusual circumstance.
4ab752c470aa9fbe79ce: This authority does not exist to set the Game Master against the players.
28a5be4f1ed2ee0bd200: It lets the game continue even when someone tries something that no manual could anticipate.
d7c12b6e578586c9632f: The GM does not play against the crew
c27977ab9a22aabaa378: The Game Master controls the opponents, but this does not mean their objective is to defeat the players.
7b269b05df29f379d09e: An enemy may want to win.
f28066532745d8cae559: Their task is to have that enemy act consistently with who they are.
a44351730de0d65b3414: A proud fighter might accept a head-on confrontation.
7fbc909671dc3396f055: A sniper might avoid any close confrontation.
059eb1ea7e5f9314cce7: An officer might order a retreat if the situation becomes desperate.
c3e74a7d15044abf8da0: A hungry creature might stop fighting as soon as it finds something more interesting to devour.
e829fb7be68374edc0dd: Player and character do not always have the same information.
09e5e6eb5bf7895510e4: A player might immediately realise that a particular creature is dangerous.
6cf1e7dc94022a2bf20b: Their character might never have seen it.
ac1770fcd93ec347a35f: Likewise, the Game Master knows what is behind a door, but the inhabitants of the world do not necessarily know.
2893d4f3a342ae2a4a94: Separating what the player knows from what the character knows helps keep the story coherent.
aa7798b4d64499f40be3: When there is doubt, the GM can ask for an appropriate check to determine how much the character actually knows.
bde5a1c7b6d7329d458b: The rules represent what happens in the world.
bd770a0605db1860080f: They are not two separate layers.
72a47dec8aacbde043de: If a Technique pushes an opponent three metres, that enemy is actually hurled backwards in the story.
2da9036c6b204e219c55: If a character runs out of Stamina, that expenditure represents exertion with concrete consequences.
d671448ccafbacf8af46: If the ship takes damage, that damage exists in the world and can require repairs.
52f1f701decf223812a0: For this reason, a good description must not contradict the result of the rules.
fd2cdef0111e795e7df8: It must turn that result into something the table can imagine.
d172c90d791561e3d080: The Game Master builds the world.
598bfe71e4c627d66617: The rules determine what happens when neither can simply decide the outcome.
aac9ac8c520dacaadf84: When these three elements work together, the game ceases to be a story told to a group of people.
993d4012c603d2fef639: It becomes a story that nobody at the table could have written alone.
5bf7eb2f34a4151bc95e: The mechanical heart of Grand Line Chronicles is the Will of D. System.
4efbb3ffa5f422608c25: Whenever an action's outcome is uncertain, the game translates the character's ability, experience and specialisation into dice.
ca9479d701e4199c559f: It does not merely represent higher probabilities. Above all, it represents how competent a character is at something.
71f0c156a733f8081e39: A pirate with a low value can still try a difficult action. A character with a high value, however, faces that same situation with better tools and a much more concrete chance of prevailing.
5c109192d46145a8dfd2: The system therefore does not use large quantities of numerical modifiers that must constantly be added together. The main form of growth directly advances the die associated with an ability.
456c242ef7126437a365: Each step on the scale represents a different level of competence.
4510b936d4e87beb69ca:
d4 · Basic
The character has elementary knowledge or an ability that is still underdeveloped.
c90b7bce501e591a2768:
d6 · Competent
They can use that ability reliably in ordinary situations.
2bd9159b407fa5f94229:
d8 · Expert
They have developed a genuine specialisation.
f426d680e7368d764908:
d10 · Master
The ability has become one of their main strengths.
1998c9b3a604f3547ddd:
d12 · Legend
Very few individuals reach this level.
3c8c42deddcede7bb6f5:
d20 · Mythic
This represents abilities beyond the normal scale, worthy of the Grand Line's most extraordinary characters.
f27c9316a277c5cd449f: These Grades appear in almost every part of the game.
22e241643cfba02986ce: Attributes, Skills, Techniques, weapons, Haki, Devil Fruits and numerous other systems use the same scale.
2d2f949eb827e930c7b5: The player therefore needs to learn just one mathematical language, which they will encounter everywhere.
db0725d8870eeb8d8f5b: A check can use several dice when different abilities contribute to the same action.
eda1fbaa54e4646d57e2: For example, a character might tackle a situation using an Attribute together with an appropriate Skill.
ba7f0f4f0c3d98a47f5f: In combat, a Technique can become part of the roll.
19990d44b396459873a7: A weapon can use its own Grade.
b719e9ec5eeb2a4b3fd7: Other systems can add dice or modify how they are rolled.
40ee74956641bf8e05c6: The exact composition depends on the situation and is explained in the relevant chapters.
bc88ada3c16e740a077b: The principle, however, always remains the same:
c947e06495d7715435d5: each die must represent something the character is actually using.
7071165ad490e8e5e703: You do not add a die because “a bonus is needed”.
ce7f371616546b604ec8: You add it because a concrete ability contributes to the action.
26f7171ce23dac550542: Additional dice with no specified type
6f532c7958082f98559b: When a rule grants +1 die or several additional dice without specifying their type, use the die that serves as the main reference for the action or effect.
62ff32b10942a49ff3b6: In a normal Check based on Attribute + Skill, the reference die is normally the Attribute unless the ability states otherwise.
a16bcc6297632e18eabd: If, instead, the action or effect explicitly uses a Skill, Weapon Grade, Technique Die, Damage Die, Fruit Die, Haki Die or another specific die as its reference, the additional die is a new copy of that die.
0ddfcf9f2b76fc01ed05: A generic +1 die does not mean repeating the entire pool and does not automatically add all the dice making up the action.
5c135d4a5f047c5deb83: Additional dice obtained through Prestige are not duplicated by this rule unless explicitly stated.
4387a2cd2775b97f08d5: When a rule states −1 die, a die is not physically removed from the pool. Instead, the reference die is reduced by one Grade along the normal scale:
0802c0b2b97ee2b817d0: The d4 is the minimum limit and cannot be reduced further by a normal Grade reduction.
